text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a sharp rise in outbound failures from gpu-fleet nodes in us-west-2. App errors show `connect: connection refused` and S3 fetches timing out. Alert (sre-bot) flagged NAT gateway high ephemeral ports at 1717364700.

sre-bot: ALERT: NAT-GW-prod-usw2-1 ephemeral_ports_in_use > 62k (threshold 61k) — potential port exhaustion. See metrics link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/9842 :rotating_light:

Maya: Confirming. Lots of ImagePullBackOff and model-registry fetch failures. I see `ss -s` on node shows lots of TIME_WAIT.

Noah: Quick dump from one node: ```
# ss -t state TIME-WAIT sport 52345 dst 52.216.12.34:443
TIME-WAIT: 25401
ESTAB: 123
```

Li: Those TIME_WAITs combined with many concurrent short connections to the same S3 endpoints will exhaust source ports on the NAT. AWS NAT gateway has a finite ephemeral port pool per elastic IP. We're hitting that.

alex: Root cause hypothesis: our GPU jobs spin up many short-lived workers that call out to S3/model-registry for small files in parallel. Each worker opens new TCP connections without reusing keep-alive. With 2k pods per AZ this multiplies.

Maya: Immediate impact: degraded tail latency and API 5xx for some customers. Ops page shows elevated retries from infra layer.

ops-oncall: Temporary mitigation applied: increased NAT gateway count for prod us-west-2 from 1->3 (attached to subnets). Also added additional Elastic IPs on the NATs. Should give more port capacity in the short term.

Noah: Recommended medium-term fixes: 1) enable HTTP connection pooling at client level (keep-alive, longer keepalive timeout) 2) use an egress proxy in the VPC (nginx/httpx) to multiplex outbound connections 3) move heavy external traffic to VPC endpoints (S3 gateway) to avoid NAT entirely 4) break up simultaneous startup storms with jitter/backoff.

Maya: Also consider per-AZ NATs to avoid cross-AZ bottlenecks and using ENI-specific private IPs to increase port space. We'll also add more subnets + NAT per AZ as a resilient config.

Li: Action items I can own: - Add egress-proxy helm chart to infra-staging for testing (nginx + connection pool, http2) - Instrument client libs to surface `conn_reuse` metric - Add Grafana panel for ephemeral_port_utilization per NAT EIP

alex: Ops has scheduled a rollout: temporary NAT scale now, deploy egress-proxy to canary nodes in staging tomorrow, and planning a cluster-level change to reduce connection churn. No config/secret changes required for canary.

Maya: One gotcha — some internal clients rely on ephemeral source IP for external allowlist. If we consolidate through a single proxy we'll need to update security teams. Noted in the rollout doc.

ops-oncall: Monitoring: added alert condition to page at 60k and automated runbook with steps: scale nat, check ss -s, grep TIME-WAIT, enable keepalive on offending service config. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/ops/nat-port-exhaustion

Noah: Long term: explore AWS PrivateLink for model-registry and S3 Gateway endpoints, and evaluate keeping model artifacts in the VPC (EFS/FSx) for hot reads to avoid external egress for each worker.

alex: Thanks team. Marking this resolved for now since NAT scaled and errors dropped ~80%. Keeping this open for follow-ups (egress-proxy test + client keepalive).

Maya: Follow-ups: I'll open a PR for client lib keepalive defaults and schedule a 2-hour window to test proxy in staging next week. :+1:
